question: What happened in the YieldBlox/Reflector oracle-manipulation incident, roughly how much was lost/recovered, and what are the design lessons?

golden.answer: On 2026-02-22 an attacker pumped the thin USTRY/USDC Stellar DEX market from about $1.06 to $106. Reflector's five-minute VWAP feed published the fresh manipulated price, and the community YieldBlox Blend V2 pool accepted it as collateral, so the attacker borrowed about 61.2M XLM and 1M USDC (roughly $10M, valuations differ by source). Validators quarantined about 48M XLM, which is not recovery. Reflector, Blend core and Stellar were not compromised. Defenses are market-depth minimums, value bounds and supply caps on thin collateral.
keyFacts: A 2026-02-22 USTRY price pump fed through Reflector's VWAP drained a YieldBlox pool.
About 61.2M XLM and 1M USDC were borrowed; dollar loss (~$10M) varies by source.
About 48M XLM was quarantined by validators; quarantine is not recovery.
Staleness was not causal; depth minimums, value bounds and supply caps are defenses.
avoid: Do NOT call the quarantined XLM recovered, or assert attacker repayment without proof.
Do NOT claim Reflector, Blend core, Etherfuse or Stellar protocol was compromised.
Do NOT present 1,014,196.7040837 USDC as a single borrow transaction.
golden.notes: Do not require an exact dollar figure. Script3's ~$10M (2026-02-22) and ~$10.5M net (2026-03-04) are both acceptable when attributed.

truth.notes:
2026-06-29 reviewed; rubric correctly gates on the approximate-range/reconcile discipline, not one exact figure. Freshness:true; figures approximate. RECONCILED across dated sources (2026-02): loss ~$10.2M (range to ~$10.86M; some say $10.8M); ~48,069,094 XLM (~$7.2M–$7.5M) frozen by Tier-1 validators ~Feb 22; date Feb 21–22 (~00:25 UTC Feb 22). Vector: USTRY (Etherfuse US-Treasury Stablebond) pumped ~$1.06→~$106 on illiquid SDEX, poisoning Reflector's VWAP feed; attacker borrowed ~61.25M XLM + ~1M USDC. Pool-operator/oracle config failure, NOT a Blend V2 core or Stellar-protocol flaw; Script3 reports supplier remediation (2026-02-27) and backstop remediation (2026-03-20), with no remediation for liquidated users; recovery of attacker-held funds remains unverified. Don't gate on one exact $.
Also good if the answer: Ties USTRY (an Etherfuse US-Treasury Stablebond) priced on illiquid SDEX into the Reflector VWAP oracle as the manipulation vector; attacker borrowed ~61M XLM + ~1M USDC. | Frames it as a pool-operator/oracle-config failure, NOT a Blend V2 core-contract or Stellar-protocol flaw.
Golden cites: A dated Scout / news source for the incident and the loss/recovery figures.
CORRECTION 2026-07-10 (GT-09 processes 3226/3235): require separate labels for token borrow, dated gross valuation, operator net loss, defaults, validator quarantine, remediation, and recovery. About 48M quarantined is safe; the exact Blockaid number must stay attributed. Recovery remains unverified. Staleness was not causal; never promise TWAP alone.
CORRECTION 2026-11-02: Script3's 2026-03-04 post-mortem lists a separate 14,000 USDC attacker borrow (tx 01c2ba75…, 00:20:50 UTC; Horizon confirms) and a ~$10.5M net-loss estimate. SLP-0006 froze the three exploit accounts in network configuration at ledger 63073409 (2026-06-17). Accept 1.01M USDC as total borrowed; still reject it as one transaction. Script3 gave two dated figures: about $10M loss (2026-02-22 X post) and about $10.5M net loss (2026-03-04 post-mortem); do not penalize either when attributed. The $10.97M figure is rekt.news's own valuation, not a Script3 statement.
